body: The Northrop B-2 Spirit is not built for comfort. It is built to survive the first night of a war, penetrating enemy air defences to carry out opening strikes, and the US Air Force often flies it nonstop from its home base at Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri, refuelling from tankers along the way to avoid leaving the aircraft exposed on the ground. Twenty-one B-2s were built and 19 remain in service. Missions can last more than 40 hours: the longest, in October 2001 during Operation Enduring Freedom, spent around 44 hours in the air and 70 hours in total including a crew change at an overseas base; Operation Midnight Hammer against Iran's Fordow facility in June 2025 lasted around 37 hours in the air, while missions to Kosovo in 1999 and Iraq in 2003 lasted around 31 and 33 hours.

Behind the cockpit the aircraft has rudimentary combat rest facilities: a basic, portable, sealed chemical toilet, with minimal privacy, and a fold-down sleep cot mounted along the cockpit bulkhead, for one pilot at a time. The cot is not long enough for tall pilots to stretch out fully, and it is meant for functional naps rather than deep rest. Pilots also bring pre-packed meals on board. The B-2 has a crew of two, the pilot in the left seat and the mission commander in the right, and the cockpit is high enough for a 6-foot-tall pilot to stand up.

The widely repeated story that the B-2 carries a mini-fridge and a microwave is mostly overblown. B-2 pilot Tim Sutton said in a 2023 interview that the aircraft had been upgraded with a microwave for heating food, while The Atlantic reported that the supposed mini-fridge is typically a couple of Styrofoam coolers containing food the pilots pack for themselves, and that pilots have stretched out on the floor in the back of the cockpit to nap. In 2019, former B-52 pilot Chris Beck, a graduate of B-2 pilot school, told Defense News that once crews get used to ultra-long missions, anything under 20 hours does not seem like a big deal, and that pilots take naps of a couple of hours. Whiteman Air Force Base has doctors and physiologists who specialise in how prolonged flying affects the human body, and doctors will prescribe medication on especially long missions to help pilots stay focused.
en.summary: Simple Flying looks at how the B-2 Spirit keeps its two-person crew going on missions lasting more than 40 hours: a fold-down cot and a basic chemical toilet behind the cockpit, pre-packed meals, and a mini-fridge and microwave legend that is mostly overblown.
en.title: Inside the B-2 Spirit's crew rest areas: a fold-down cot, a chemical toilet and the microwave legend

body: B-2匿蹤轟炸機不是為舒適而設計，而是為了在戰爭首夜穿透敵方防空網、執行開場打擊；為了避免在地面被摧毀，美軍往往讓B-2自密蘇里州懷特曼空軍基地直飛任務區，再由空中加油機沿途加油。全機共生產21架，現役19架；任務動輒超過40小時：2001年10月持久自由行動的任務在空中飛行約44小時，全程含更換機組共70小時；2025年6月午夜鐵鎚行動打擊伊朗福爾多核設施時，B-2在空中飛行約37小時；1999年科索沃任務約31小時，2003年伊拉克自由行動約33小時。
駕駛艙後方設有簡陋的戰鬥休息設施：一具可攜式密封化學馬桶，隱私極少；一張沿駕駛艙隔板安裝的折疊帆布床，一次僅供一名飛行員使用，長度不足以讓高個子飛行員完全伸展，僅供功能性小睡而非深度休息；機組員另攜帶預先打包的餐食。B-2機組僅兩人，分別為左座飛行員與右座任務指揮官，駕駛艙高度足以讓身高6英尺的飛行員站立。

網路盛傳B-2配有迷你冰箱與微波爐，真相介於傳聞與現實之間：B-2飛行員Tim Sutton在2023年受訪時表示，機上已加裝微波爐加熱食物；至於迷你冰箱，據《大西洋月刊》報導，通常只是飛行員自行攜帶食物的幾個保麗龍冷藏箱，另有飛行員直接躺在駕駛艙後方地板上小睡。曾任B-52飛行員、後畢業於B-2飛行員學校的Chris Beck在2019年受訪時表示，機組習慣超長任務後，20小時以下的任務便不算什麼，飛行員通常小睡數小時；懷特曼基地甚至配有專門研究長時間飛行對人體影響的醫師與生理學家，超長任務時還會開立藥物幫助飛行員保持專注。
zh.summary: Simple Flying介紹B-2轟炸機在動輒40小時以上的任務中如何讓兩名機組員輪流休息：駕駛艙後方僅有折疊帆布床、簡易化學馬桶與預先打包的餐食，所謂迷你冰箱與微波爐的傳說，多半被誇大了。
zh.title: B-2匿蹤轟炸機的機組休息區：折疊帆布床、化學馬桶與微波爐傳說
